title: The Value of Human Frailty: Nvidia faces a Jensen Test!
description:
The story of Jensen Huang's first affair, with Alice Wu, broke on October 29, 2026, and its mix of personal foibles and security issues, has made it a front page story around the world. The revelation that Jensen had other affairs with Nvidia employees forced the board's hand and he stepped down on November 12. No matter what you think of that action, and there are supporter and critics, even Jensen's strongest opponents should concede that he has be an exceptional CEO, a founder who built a company in his image, and made it not only one of the world's most valuable firms, but also been a key part of the AI boom. In this session, I start with a general question of what CEOs do at companies, and use it to look at when CEOs matter the most to the companies they lead. I follow up with a framework to value CEOs, and  use that framework to value the effect of the Jensen Huang scandal on Nvidia. The value effect will be a function of (a) whether Jensen gets reinstated as CEO (a low probability), (b) how good the replacement CEO is, (c) how well Jensen will work with the replacement CEO, (d) how good Nvidia's second-layer management is and (d) whether the China twist to the story has legs. The bottom line is that the $1.5 trillion meltdown in Nvidia's market cap is creating an opportunity for investors who are willing to live with the uncertainties to enter the stock.

summary: The speaker argues that while Nvidia faces a specific 'Jensen Test' where short-term value could drop by 24% if growth slows and margins compress, the company remains fundamentally undervalued at its current price. He believes the stock is a bargain because it possesses an extraordinary capacity to scale while preserving high margins, driven by an incredibly effective CEO. However, the investment case is mixed, as the outcome depends heavily on whether the transition of leadership remains smooth and the China scandal does not have lasting negative effects.

claims.claim: The speaker believes short-term value drops are likely but contained, while long-term effects depend on revenue growth and margin changes, with a potential 24% value drop if growth drops 3% and margins drop 6%.
claims.quote: I get about 5 to 10% drop in value from the 4.8 8 trillion which would mean that at 3.6 trillion it looks cheap but there potentially could be long-term effects and the long-term effects show up in two places and these are the two key inputs. One is as a drop in revenue growth and the other is as a drop in margin. So everything you think of as a consequence is going to show up in one of those two places.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker calculates that a 3% drop in revenue growth and a 6% drop in margins would cause Nvidia's value to drop by 24%.
claims.quote: So as an example, if you have a 3% drop in re grow drop in revenue growth and a 6% drop in margins, Nvidia's value drops by 24%.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker advises that if a competent replacement CEO is found, Jensen Huang stays involved, and the China scandal is overblown, the value drop will be small and the market will recover.
claims.quote: If you do think that the board will find a competent replacement CEO match a CEO matches where you are where Invidia is in the life cycle that Jensen will stay involved and work with that CEO and that there's a strong management team and on top of that you throw in the China twist is overblown the value drop will be small so market will recover from the 3.6 trillion back maybe not to the 5.2 two trillion but to a higher number.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker warns that if the process becomes ugly, the new CEO has frictions with Jensen Huang, and the China scandal has legs, the value drop might get worse.
claims.quote: But if as the weeks go through the process becomes ugly and toxic and the new CEO is um has frictions with Jens and he and he burns bridges with with employees and the China scandal has legs then the value drop might get worse.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker suggests that Nvidia's travails with Jensen Huang should make investors more appreciative of founders who build companies that can outlast them and find ways to make themselves dispensable.
claims.quote: And I think we're going to get a test of how much Jensen Wong has built an entity that can outlast him in the coming weeks with what Nvidia does.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker notes that if Nvidia had two classes of shares with Jensen having 51% control of voting rights, it could turn much more toxic quickly.
claims.quote: Can you imagine if Invidia had two classes of shares and Jensen had a 51% control of the voting rights? This could turn much more toxic. much more quickly if that had happened.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker notes that until recently, Jensen Huang added value to Nvidia, though he is now facing a test regarding his role.
claims.quote: Until a few weeks ago, I think the answer to that question was obvious. Jensen Wong added value at Nvidia. I'm sure he made the top 10 list of great CEOs around the world
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker values Nvidia at $4.85 trillion based on revenue growth and margins, suggesting the stock is a bargain at its current price of $3.6 trillion.
claims.quote: In fact, if id valued Nvidia in late October, given that it had almost a doubling of revenues in the year leading in, I know this high revenues coming forward and essentially with high revenue growth, the margins they have, even as the AI building boom starts to ease, the value I would have got for the equity in the company would have been close to $4.85 trillion.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker states he likes Nvidia as an amazing company, noting it was undervalued before the scandal despite trading at a high market cap.
claims.quote: So what I want to to give up front is I like Nvidia. I think I think it's an amazing company. I just didn't like the price it was trading at. So I went back to October 29th and I valued Nvidia with Jensen Wong still CEO and no scandal on the horizon.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker believes Nvidia has an amazing capacity to scale up while preserving high profit margins, even as a large company.
claims.quote: And part of the reason is this company has shown an amazing capacity to keep scaling up even though it's a big company from 200 billion to 300 billion revenues while preserving some of the highest profit margins I've seen at a large company.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran

claims.claim: The speaker considers Jensen Huang an incredibly effective and extraordinary CEO, stating Nvidia would not be the company it is today without him.
claims.quote: Has he been an incredibly effective and extraordinary CEO? I don't think even his critics would deny him that. He's been an amazing CEO and Nvidia would not be the company it is today without him at the helm.
claims.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
